0020. Abs Snails

AbdominalsP2
Mismatch matrix

P2 · LOWER_ABS_TERM · Purpose/Steps
Uses 'lower stomach/lower abs' as if it were a separate muscle compartment.
Action: Use 'abdominals/rectus abdominis' and describe the movement (for example posterior pelvic tilt or hip flexion control) instead.

Original purpose

Rolling the hips up over the shoulders trains the lower part of the stomach through a much longer range than a crunch. It also teaches the spine to move one segment at a time instead of hinging in one place.

Original steps
  1. Lie on your back with your arms flat on the floor beside you, palms down
  2. Lift your legs until your feet point at the ceiling
  3. Press your lower back into the floor and squeeze your stomach
  4. Curl your hips off the floor and roll your legs back over your chest
  5. Lower slowly, one part of the spine at a time, until your hips touch down again
Proposed variant
Purpose: Trains the abdominals and trunk control through the Abs Snails movement. Use a controlled range and keep the movement symptom-free.
Steps: No deterministic step rewrite required. Follow the Action note above for judgment-based changes.

Original purpose

Trains rotation at full speed, which is how the trunk works in almost every sport — a golf swing, a punch, a throw. Slow twisting exercises build the strength; this teaches the body to use it quickly.

  1. Stand side-on to a solid wall, about a metre away, holding a medicine ball

0227. Barbell Coan Deadlift

BackPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

A deadlift done with the hips set higher and the bar dragged close, which shifts the work onto the upper back and hamstrings. It is a strength-sport variation — take it up only once a normal deadlift is comfortable and repeatable.

Original steps
  1. Stand with the bar over your mid-foot, feet about hip width apart
  2. Grip the bar just outside your knees and set your hips higher than in a normal deadlift
  3. Pull the slack out of the bar and lock your upper back tight before anything moves
  4. Push the floor away and drag the bar up your shins, keeping it touching your legs
  5. Stand fully upright, then lower along the same path without rounding your back

0237. Barbell Reverse Deadlift

BackP2
Mismatch matrix

P2 · PRIOR_REAUDIT · Purpose/Steps
REV2 changed this card, but the edit does not close every prior finding. Keep the unresolved prior action(s) below.
Action: Prefer 'brace and maintain a stable/neutral spine' unless posterior pelvic tilt/bench contact is intentionally required.; Use 'move through the largest controlled, pain-free range you can maintain without compensation.'

Original purpose

Starting from the top and lowering first teaches the hip hinge without the hardest part — breaking the bar off the floor. Good for learning the movement and for loading the lowering phase, where most of the muscle is built.

Original steps
  1. Set the bar in a rack at hip height and take it with an overhand grip, standing tall
  2. Push your hips back and let the bar slide down the front of your thighs
  3. Keep your spine neutral and your shins upright as the bar passes your knees
  4. Lower until you feel a strong stretch behind the thighs, then touch the floor if you can reach it
  5. Drive your hips forward to stand back up, finishing tall without leaning back
Proposed variant
Purpose: Trains the back and trunk muscles through the Barbell Reverse Deadlift movement. Keep the torso controlled and use a range you can maintain without compensation.

0257. Cable Lat Prayer

BackPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

Isolates the lats with the arms nearly straight, so the biceps cannot take over the way they do on every row and pulldown. This is the exercise for people who pull a lot and still never feel their back working.

Original steps
  1. Set a rope on the high pulley and kneel a step back from the machine
  2. Take both ends overhead with the arms almost straight and a small bend in the elbows
  3. Sit your hips back slightly and lengthen through the spine
  4. Pull the rope down in a wide arc toward your thighs without bending the elbows further
  5. Let the arms rise slowly back overhead until you feel the lats stretch

A pull-up that uses a hip swing to help the arms, which lets you do far more repetitions for conditioning. It trains rhythm and grip endurance rather than pure back strength — do strict pull-ups first, and only kip once you have them.

BackP1
Mismatch matrix

Original purpose

Holds the hips up with the glutes while the lats work overhead, so the front of your body is stretched open at both ends. A useful counter to a day spent folded forward at a desk.

Original steps
  1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, holding a plate over your chest
  2. Lift your hips into a bridge and keep the glutes squeezed for the whole set
  3. With slightly bent arms, lower the plate back over your head toward the floor
  4. Go only as far as you can without your ribs lifting or your hips dropping
  5. Pull the plate back over your chest using the lats, keeping the bridge held

  4. Go only through the largest controlled, pain-free range you can maintain without compensation without your ribs lifting or your hips dropping

0331. Plate Pinch Grip Deadlift

BackPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

Pinching two plates between the fingers and thumb trains a grip that a hook or a strap can never build. Grip is the first thing to fail on heavy rows, carries and pull-ups, so it is worth training on its own.

Original steps
  1. Stand two plates together on the floor with the smooth sides facing outward
  2. Stand over them with your feet either side, hips back and spine neutral
  3. Pinch the outer faces with your fingers and thumb — no hooking the rim
  4. Stand up by driving through the legs, keeping the plates hanging still
  5. Hold at the top for a few seconds, then lower under control before your grip fails
Proposed variant

0332. Plate Pinch Grip Row

Original purpose

A back row and a grip test in one: the pinch hold fails long before the back does, so every rep is fighting to keep hold. Best used late in a session when heavy rowing is already done.

Original steps
  1. Hinge forward with a neutral spine, holding a plate pinched in each hand by its smooth face
  2. Let both plates hang straight down under your shoulders
  3. Brace your stomach and hold the torso still
  4. Row both plates to your ribs, keeping the pinch tight
  5. Lower them slowly to arms' length and repeat until the grip, not the back, stops you

BackP2

Original purpose

The machine supports your chest and lower back, so you can pull heavy without your spine having to hold the position. That makes it one of the lower-back-friendlier ways to row heavy, and the one to choose when the lower back is already tired.

Original steps
  1. Set the seat height so the handles line up with the middle of your chest
  2. Sit with your chest against the pad and your feet planted
  3. Take the handles with your arms straight and shoulder blades relaxed forward
  4. Pull the handles to your ribs, driving the elbows back and squeezing the blades together
  5. Return slowly until the arms are straight and the blades open again

Trains the muscles that run along the spine to hold a position under load — the exact job they do during a deadlift or a heavy carry. A strong set of these is one of the better insurances against a back that gives out.

Original steps

0379. Alternate Biceps Curl Resistance Band

BicepsPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

Works one arm at a time so the stronger side cannot quietly take over, which is what happens on every two-handed curl. A band keeps tension on the biceps at the top of the movement, where a dumbbell goes light and the muscle gets a rest it did not earn.

Original steps
  1. Stand on the middle of the band with feet hip width apart and hold one end in each hand, palms forward
  2. Keep your elbows pinned against your ribs and your shoulders down
  3. Curl one hand up toward the shoulder, letting the band stretch, and keep the other arm straight
  4. Lower that hand under control all the way down before the other arm starts
  5. Alternate arms for the whole set, never letting the elbows drift forward

Original purpose

The plainest way to build the biceps and the one every other curl is measured against. Alternating halves the load on your torso at any moment, so you can stand upright and let the arm do the work instead of swinging the weight up with your back.

Original steps

0427. Cable Twisting Biceps Curl

BicepsPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

Turning the palm outward as you curl is what the biceps actually does — it bends the elbow and rotates the forearm, and most curls only ask for half of that. The cable holds tension through the whole path, including the turn, which a free weight cannot do.

Original steps
  1. Set a single handle on the lowest pulley and stand facing the machine, one step back
  2. Take the handle with your palm facing your thigh and let your arm hang straight
  3. Curl upward and rotate your palm to face the ceiling as the elbow bends
  4. Finish with the hand at shoulder height and the palm fully turned up, elbow still at your side
  5. Reverse both movements slowly — unbend and untwist together — then repeat
Proposed variant
Purpose: No purpose rewrite required by the targeted patterns.
Steps: No deterministic step rewrite required. Follow the Action note above for judgment-based changes.

0468. Dumbbell Seated Zottman Curl

BicepsP2
Mismatch matrix

P2 · PRIOR_REAUDIT · Purpose/Steps
This card was not materially changed in REV2 for the prior finding(s); the previous finding remains open.
Action: Use neutral wording about the movement/muscles; avoid claiming one exercise reverses a lifestyle/postural problem without assessment.

Original purpose

One exercise that trains both sides of the arm: you lift with the palm up, which loads the biceps, and lower with the palm down, which loads the forearm. Sitting removes the leg drive, so nothing but the arms moves the weight.

Original steps
  1. Sit on the end of a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging, palms forward
  2. Curl both dumbbells up to your shoulders with your elbows fixed at your sides
  3. At the top, rotate your wrists so the palms now face the floor
  4. Lower the dumbbells slowly in that position — this half should feel harder and take longer
  5. At the bottom, rotate the palms forward again and start the next repetition
Proposed variant
Purpose: Trains elbow flexion and the biceps through the Dumbbell Seated Zottman Curl movement. Keep the upper arm controlled and use a load you can move without swinging.
Steps: No deterministic step rewrite required. Follow the Action note above for judgment-based changes.

0494. Kettlebell Concentration Curl

BicepsPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

Bracing the elbow against the inside of the thigh removes every way of cheating — you cannot swing, lean back or shrug the weight up. What is left is the biceps alone, which is why this is the exercise people use when an arm is visibly lagging.

Original steps
  1. Sit on a bench with your feet wide and lean forward slightly from the hips
  2. Hold the kettlebell in one hand and brace the back of that upper arm against the inside of the same thigh
  3. Let the arm hang straight down so the bell is just off the floor
  4. Curl the bell up toward your shoulder without letting the elbow leave the thigh
  5. Lower all the way until the arm is straight, then repeat and switch sides
Proposed variant

0495. Kettlebell Curl

BicepsP2
Mismatch matrix

P2 · PRIOR_REAUDIT · Purpose/Steps
Accepted exception: 'grip training you get for free' is ordinary idiom for an incidental training effect, not a safety or medical promise. No content change required for this phrase.
Action: Re-review this card before H3 propagation.

Original purpose

The bell hangs below your hand rather than sitting in it, so the weight pulls the wrist backwards the whole way up. Your forearm has to work to keep the wrist straight, which is grip training you get for free alongside the biceps.

Original steps
  1. Stand with a kettlebell in each hand, handles gripped so the bells hang in front of your thighs
  2. Keep your wrists straight and locked — do not let the bells bend them back
  3. Curl both bells up toward your shoulders with the elbows against your sides
  4. Stop when your forearms are vertical and the bells rest against your forearms
  5. Lower under control to full arm extension before the next repetition
Proposed variant
Purpose: Trains elbow flexion and the biceps through the Kettlebell Curl movement. Keep the upper arm controlled and use a load you can move without swinging.
Steps: No deterministic step rewrite required. Follow the Action note above for judgment-based changes.

Original purpose

The pad under your arm stops the elbow from travelling, which is the one thing that lets the shoulder help on a standing curl. With that route closed the biceps has to finish the lift from the hardest position — arm nearly straight.

Original steps
  1. Set the preacher bench so the top of the pad sits under your armpit when you sit down
  2. Lay the back of one upper arm flat along the pad and hold the kettlebell in that hand
  3. Straighten the arm until you feel the stretch, but do not let the elbow lock hard
  4. Curl the bell up toward your shoulder, keeping the arm glued to the pad
  5. Lower slowly to the stretched position and repeat, then change arms

0551. Ball Slams

P2 · PRIOR_REAUDIT · Purpose/Steps

Original purpose

Throwing a ball into the ground as hard as you can trains the whole body to produce force fast, and it is one of the few exercises where you can go completely all out safely. Also a very effective way to raise the heart rate.

  1. Stand with your feet shoulder width apart holding the ball at your chest
  2. Raise the ball overhead, extending fully onto your toes
  3. Brace your stomach and slam the ball down into the floor as hard as you can
  4. Follow through by hinging at the hips, keeping your spine neutral
  5. Pick the ball up and repeat immediately for the set

Original purpose

Pushing weight with no lowering phase means less of the muscle damage a normal lower-body session leaves behind, so you can push hard here without it eating into recovery for your next leg day.

Original steps
  1. Load the box and grip the high handles or the frame
  2. Lean your body forward at about forty-five degrees with straight arms
  3. Keep your spine neutral and your head in line with your spine
  4. Drive through the balls of your feet with short powerful steps
  5. Push for the set distance, then rest fully before the next run
Proposed variant
Purpose: Develops strength, coordination or conditioning through Box Sled Push. Use a load and speed that allow controlled technique throughout the movement.
Steps:
  1. Place both hands firmly on the box or block at about chest height.
  2. Lean your body forward with straight but not forcefully locked arms and brace your trunk.
  3. Maintain a stable, neutral spine with your head in line with your torso.
  4. Drive the box forward with short, powerful steps while keeping the whole foot controlled against the floor.
  5. Push for the set distance, then stop under control and rest before the next effort.

Original purpose

Builds shoulder strength and whole-body control in a way nothing else does, and it improves the sense of where your body is in space. Learn it against a wall first, and never on a hard floor without a plan for coming down.

Original steps
  1. Place your hands on the floor about shoulder width apart, a foot from a wall
  2. Kick one leg up and then the other so your heels rest on the wall
  3. Push the floor away, lock your elbows and squeeze your glutes and stomach
  4. Stack your hips over your shoulders and look between your hands
  5. Hold for as long as your line stays straight, then come down one leg at a time

Original purpose

Pulling a sled toward you hand over hand works the whole back with no lowering phase at all, so you can do a lot of it without paying for it the next day. Grip and lungs usually run out first.

  1. Attach a rope to a loaded sled and sit or stand at the far end
  2. Take the rope in both hands and set your feet firmly
  3. Brace your stomach and keep your spine neutral
  4. Pull the rope hand over hand, drawing the sled toward you
  5. Keep pulling without pausing until the sled reaches you, then reset

Original purpose

Jumping from one leg trains power on a single limb, which is how running and most sport actually happen. Use a low box — the landing is what matters, and height only adds risk here.

Original steps
  1. Stand on one leg in front of a low box with the knee slightly bent
  2. Dip and swing your arms back to load the leg
  3. Jump up onto the box, landing on the same foot
  4. Absorb the landing softly with the knee tracking over the toes
  5. Step down carefully, reset, and repeat before changing legs

0752. Barbell Hooklying Bench Press

ChestP2
Mismatch matrix

P2 · PRIOR_REAUDIT · Purpose/Steps
This card was not materially changed in REV2 for the prior finding(s); the previous finding remains open.
Action: Prefer 'brace and maintain a stable/neutral spine' unless posterior pelvic tilt/bench contact is intentionally required.

Original purpose

Pressing with your feet up and knees bent takes the arch out of your lower back, so nothing but the chest, shoulders and arms can move the bar. Useful when your back is sore and a normal bench press means bracing through it.

Original steps
  1. Lie on a bench and lift your feet, knees bent above your hips, shins roughly parallel to the floor
  2. Press your lower back flat into the bench and keep it there
  3. Unrack the bar and hold it over your chest with arms straight
  4. Lower the bar to your mid-chest with the elbows at about forty-five degrees
  5. Press it back up without letting your back arch or your feet drop
Proposed variant

0753. Barbell Hooklying Bench Press Close Elbows

ChestP2
Mismatch matrix

P2 · PRIOR_REAUDIT · Purpose/Steps
This card was not materially changed in REV2 for the prior finding(s); the previous finding remains open.
Action: Prefer 'brace and maintain a stable/neutral spine' unless posterior pelvic tilt/bench contact is intentionally required.

Original purpose

The same back-protecting position, with the elbows kept in against the ribs so the triceps takes the larger share and the front of the shoulder is spared. This is the version to use if a wide press makes the shoulder ache.

Original steps
  1. Lie on the bench with your feet up and knees bent above your hips
  2. Flatten your lower back into the bench and hold it there
  3. Unrack the bar with your hands about shoulder width apart
  4. Lower it toward the lower part of your chest, keeping your elbows brushing your sides
  5. Press back up in a straight line, elbows staying tucked the whole way

0756. Barbell Landmine Chest Press

ChestPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

Presses on an upward arc rather than straight out, which keeps the shoulder in a position it likes and lets you press hard without a bench or a spotter. Often the first pressing movement people can return to after a shoulder problem.

Original steps
  1. Load one end of a barbell in the landmine and stand facing away from the anchor
  2. Bring the loaded end up to the front of one shoulder and cup it with that hand
  3. Stand in a short split stance and squeeze your stomach and glutes
  4. Press the bar up and forward until the arm is straight, following its arc
  5. Return it to your shoulder under control, then finish the set and switch sides
Proposed variant

0757. Barbell Larsen Bench Press

ChestPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

Feet flat but out in front, so you cannot drive with your legs at all. Whatever weight you press here is what your upper body can genuinely do — which is why lifters use it to find out how much of their bench was leg drive.

Original steps
  1. Lie on a bench and place your feet flat on the floor well in front of your knees
  2. Keep your hips and shoulders on the bench with a normal, not exaggerated, arch
  3. Unrack the bar and hold it above your chest
  4. Lower it to your chest under control without pushing through your feet
  5. Press it back up using only your upper body — the legs stay passive throughout

0763. Barbell Spoto Press

ChestPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

Stopping the bar an inch above the chest removes the bounce, so you have to start the press from a dead stop in the weakest position. It is the standard fix for a bench press that stalls just off the chest.

Original steps
  1. Set up on the bench as you would for a normal press and unrack the bar
  2. Lower it under control until it is roughly two or three centimetres above your chest
  3. Stop there and hold for a full second — the bar must not touch you
  4. Press it back up without any bounce or momentum
  5. Reset at the top and repeat, keeping the pause the same length every rep
Proposed variant

ChestP1
Mismatch matrix

Purpose implies the floor press avoids the shoulder position that irritates a sore shoulder. Better: the floor limits shoulder extension versus a bench press; users with shoulder pain should use a comfortable range or seek assessment.

P1 · MEDICAL_CLAIM · Purpose/Steps
Uses rehabilitation, pain-treatment, injury-prevention or symptom language that can read as a therapeutic promise rather than fitness coaching.
Action: Describe the training target. If rehab is mentioned, qualify it as clinician-led and avoid promising symptom relief or injury prevention.

Original purpose

The floor stops your elbows before the shoulder reaches the end of its range, so you get most of the pressing work with none of the position that irritates a sore shoulder. It also needs no bench at all.

Original steps
  1. Lie on your back on the floor with knees bent and feet flat, a dumbbell in each hand
  2. Press the dumbbells up over your chest until your arms are straight
  3. Lower them until the backs of your upper arms touch the floor
  4. Pause there for a moment rather than bouncing off the floor
  5. Press back up, keeping your lower back in contact with the ground
Proposed variant

Mismatch matrix

Original purpose

One side at a time, so the chest has to both open the arm and stop your body rolling toward the weight. That second job is what a two-handed fly never asks for, and it is why this feels harder than the load suggests.

Original steps
  1. Lie on a bench with a kettlebell in one hand pressed above your chest, free hand on your stomach
  2. Keep a soft bend in the working elbow and hold it there
  3. Lower the bell out to the side in a wide arc until you feel the chest stretch
  4. Keep both shoulder blades flat on the bench — do not let your body roll
  5. Bring the bell back over your chest along the same arc, then change sides

0853. Kneeling Push-up

ChestP2
Mismatch matrix

P2 · SUPERLATIVE_CLAIM · Purpose
Uses a best/most/only/comparative claim without a defined population, outcome or evidence threshold.
Action: State the direct training effect, or soften to 'can', 'may', 'often', 'a useful option' and define the comparison if it matters.

Original purpose

A push-up with the load turned down: knees on the floor take roughly a third of your weight out of it. This is the honest way to build toward a full push-up, and far better than a full one done with a sagging back.

Original steps
  1. Kneel on a mat and place your hands on the floor slightly wider than your shoulders
  2. Walk your knees back until your body makes a straight line from knees to head
  3. Squeeze your stomach and glutes so your hips do not drop
  4. Bend the elbows to lower your chest toward the floor, elbows at about forty-five degrees
  5. Push back up to straight arms without letting the hips lead
Proposed variant
Purpose: Trains the chest, shoulders and triceps through the Kneeling Push-up movement. Use controlled repetitions and a range that stays comfortable at the shoulder.

Unqualified maximum-range cue may push a user beyond the range they can control without symptoms or compensation.

Original purpose

The hardest bodyweight press there is, and most of the difficulty is not in the chest — it is in refusing to rotate while one arm holds you up. Attempt it only when you can do clean full push-ups for reps.

Original steps
  1. Start in a push-up position with your feet spread wide for balance
  2. Put one hand behind your back and place the working hand under the middle of your chest
  3. Brace hard so your hips and shoulders stay square to the floor
  4. Bend the working elbow to lower your chest as far as you can control
  5. Press back up without twisting, then complete the set and change arms

0883. Band Wrist Curl Single Arm

ForearmsP2
Mismatch matrix

P2 · PRIOR_REAUDIT · Purpose/Steps
This card was not materially changed in REV2 for the prior finding(s); the previous finding remains open.
Action: Use neutral wording about the movement/muscles; avoid claiming one exercise reverses a lifestyle/postural problem without assessment.

Original purpose

Builds the wrist flexors one arm at a time, so a weaker side cannot hide behind a stronger one. Grip strength is what usually fails first on rows, deadlifts and carries, and a band loads the wrist without the joint stress of a heavy bar.

Original steps
  1. Sit and rest your forearm along your thigh, palm facing up, wrist and hand hanging past the knee
  2. Stand on one end of the band and hold the other end in that hand
  3. Let the band pull your hand down until you feel a stretch through the underside of the forearm
  4. Curl the hand upward by closing the wrist only — the forearm stays flat on the thigh
  5. Lower under control and repeat, then switch arms
Proposed variant
Purpose: Trains the forearm and grip musculature through the Band Wrist Curl Single Arm movement. Use controlled repetitions and avoid forcing the wrist into painful end range.
Steps: No deterministic step rewrite required. Follow the Action note above for judgment-based changes.

  2. Kneel or sit facing the machine and rest your forearms on a bench, hands past the edge, palms down
  3. Let the cable pull your knuckles toward the floor as far as the wrist comfortably allows
  4. Lift the knuckles toward the ceiling by extending the wrists only, forearms still on the bench
  5. Pause at the top for a moment, then lower slowly

Original purpose

  1. Sit and rest your forearm on your thigh, palm up, hand past the knee

  4. Roll it back into the palm, then curl the wrist upward as far as it goes
  5. Lower under control, keeping the forearm still throughout

0902. Kettlebell Wrist Extension

ForearmsPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

The opposite of the wrist curl, and the half most people skip. Balanced forearms keep the elbow quiet under heavy pressing and pulling, and this is the cheapest way to train the side that never gets worked by accident.

Original steps
  1. Sit and rest your forearm on your thigh, palm facing DOWN, hand past the knee
  2. Hold the kettlebell by the handle so it hangs below your hand
  3. Let the weight lower your knuckles toward the floor as far as is comfortable
  4. Raise the knuckles by extending the wrist, forearm pressed to the thigh
  5. Use a lighter bell than you would for the curl — the extensors are the smaller muscles

Original purpose

The simplest circulation exercise there is: pointing and flexing the foot pushes blood back up the leg. Used after surgery, on long flights and during any long stretch of sitting, where the calf stops acting as a pump.

Original steps
  1. Sit or lie down with your legs straight out in front of you
  2. Keep your knees relaxed and still — only the ankles move
  3. Point your toes away from you as far as they will go
  4. Pull your toes back toward your shins until you feel the calf stretch
  5. Move slowly and continue for the set time or number of repetitions
Proposed variant
Purpose: Trains the lower body through the Ankle Pumps movement. Use a controlled, pain-free range and a load that lets you keep stable alignment.

Lets you train the legs hard with your back fully supported, so there is no spinal load at all. That makes it the sensible heavy leg exercise for anyone whose back cannot take squatting.

  5. Press back out through the whole foot without locking the knees hard at the end

Original purpose

The ball held out in front acts as a counterweight, which lets most people squat deeper with a more upright back than they can empty-handed. A good way to open up squat depth before adding real load.

Original steps
  1. Hold a medicine ball at chest height with both hands, feet shoulder width apart
  2. Squat down as deep as you can while keeping your chest tall
  3. At the bottom, keep your heels down and your knees tracking over your toes
  4. Stand up and, as you rise, raise the ball overhead with straight arms
  5. Lower the ball to your chest and go straight into the next squat
Proposed variant
Purpose: Trains the lower body through the Med Ball Front Squat Raise movement. Use a controlled, pain-free range and a load that lets you keep stable alignment.
Steps:
  1. Hold a medicine ball at chest height with both hands, feet shoulder width apart
  2. Squat down to the deepest position you can control without pain or loss of alignment while keeping your chest tall

  4. Lower as far as you can control, keeping hips, chest and head aligned
  5. Pull yourself back up using the front of the thighs, not by bending at the hips

Narrow feet and raised heels point the work at the front of the thigh, and the fixed bar path lets you stay in that upright position without fighting for balance. One of the most quad-focused squat variations available.

  2. Set your feet close together, slightly in front of the bar, and unlock it
  3. Keep your chest tall and your torso as upright as the machine allows
  4. Squat straight down as deep as you can control, knees travelling forward
  5. Drive back up without letting your heels leave the wedge

1312. Barbell Hang Clean

PowerliftingPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

Teaches the body to produce force fast rather than merely to lift a lot. Starting from the hang removes the floor pull, so the whole exercise is the hip snap — the same explosive extension behind a jump, a sprint start and a throw.

Original steps
  1. Stand holding the bar at arm's length, hands just outside the hips, feet hip-width
  2. Push the hips back and slide the bar down the thighs to just above the knee, spine neutral, chest up
  3. Drive the hips forward hard and shrug — the bar is thrown upward by the legs, not pulled by the arms
  4. As it rises, drop under it and spin the elbows through to catch the bar on the front of the shoulders
  5. Stand up out of the catch, then lower the bar back to the hang and reset before the next rep
Proposed variant
Purpose: No purpose rewrite required by the targeted patterns.
Steps: No deterministic step rewrite required. Follow the Action note above for judgment-based changes.

1318. Barbell Press Under

PowerliftingPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

Drills the second half of a clean or snatch — the moment you stop pushing the bar up and start pushing yourself down under it. Most missed lifts are not a weak pull, they are a slow turnover, and this is how that gets faster.

Original steps
  1. Hold the bar at the front of the shoulders with a light load — this is a technique drill, not a strength lift
  2. Keep the bar path vertical and the torso upright throughout
  3. Press yourself DOWN under the bar rather than pressing the bar up, dropping into a quarter squat
  4. Lock the arms overhead at the same moment your hips stop descending

1330. Plate Clean

PowerliftingPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

The hip drive of a barbell clean with none of its technical cost. A plate is easier to hold, easier to bail, and lets you rehearse the explosive extension long before a loaded bar is a sensible idea.

Original steps
  1. Stand with the plate on the floor between your feet, held at its sides with both hands
  2. Hinge at the hips with a neutral spine and grip the plate low
  3. Drive through the floor and extend the hips hard, letting the plate float upward
  4. Pull yourself under it and catch it at chest height with the elbows up
  5. Lower it back to the floor under control rather than dropping it

1331. Plate Clean and Press

PowerliftingPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

One movement from the floor to overhead, so legs, trunk and shoulders have to hand the load off to each other without a pause. That handover is what makes it a conditioning exercise as much as a strength one.

Original steps
  1. Start with the plate on the floor between your feet, gripped at the sides
  2. Hinge, then extend the hips explosively and catch the plate at chest height
  3. Without resetting, brace the trunk and press the plate straight overhead
  4. Keep the ribs down — the lower back should not arch to finish the press
  5. Return the plate to the chest, then to the floor, and repeat

1332. Plate Thruster

PowerliftingP1
Mismatch matrix

P1 · PRIOR_REAUDIT · Purpose/Steps
This card was not materially changed in REV2 for the prior finding(s); the previous finding remains open.
Action: State the direct effect of the exercise without ranking it against another method.; Use 'move through the largest controlled, pain-free range you can maintain without compensation.'

P1 · FORCED_ROM · Steps
Unqualified maximum-range cue may push a user beyond the range they can control without symptoms or compensation.
Action: Use the largest controlled, pain-free range available without compensation; regress range if alignment or symptoms deteriorate.

P2 · SUPERLATIVE_CLAIM · Purpose
Uses a best/most/only/comparative claim without a defined population, outcome or evidence threshold.
Action: State the direct training effect, or soften to 'can', 'may', 'often', 'a useful option' and define the comparison if it matters.

Original purpose

A front squat and an overhead press joined into one rep, which is why it raises the heart rate faster than either alone. The legs finish the squat and the arms start the press at the same instant — that overlap is the whole point.

Original steps
  1. Hold the plate at chest height with both hands, feet shoulder-width
  2. Squat down as deep as you can while keeping the chest tall and the heels down
  3. Stand up out of the squat and, without pausing, use that momentum to press the plate overhead
  4. Lock the arms out fully with the plate over the middle of your feet
  5. Bring it back to the chest as you descend into the next rep
Proposed variant
Purpose: Builds strength and technique for Plate Thruster. Progress load only while you can maintain controlled form and stable joint positions.
Steps:
  1. Hold the plate at chest height with both hands, feet shoulder-width
  2. Squat down to the deepest position you can control without pain or loss of alignment while keeping the chest tall and the heels down
  3. Stand up out of the squat and, without pausing, use that momentum to press the plate overhead
  4. Lock the arms out fully with the plate over the middle of your feet
  5. Bring it back to the chest as you descend into the next rep

1387. Cable 30 Degree Shrug

ShouldersPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

A shrug angled forward instead of straight up, which puts the work into the part of the trapezius that runs down between the shoulder blades rather than the part that already gets used all day. That lower section is what holds the shoulder blades in place.

Original steps
  1. Set two low handles and stand facing the machine holding one in each hand
  2. Step back and lean your torso forward about thirty degrees, spine neutral
  3. Let the cables pull your shoulders forward and down at the start
  4. Shrug your shoulder blades back and down along the line of your torso, arms straight
  5. Hold the squeeze briefly, then let the blades travel forward again under control

1389. Cable Face Pull with Rope

ShouldersPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

One of the few exercises that trains the small muscles at the back of the shoulder, which get outnumbered by everything that presses. Doing these regularly is what keeps a heavy bench-press habit from slowly closing your shoulders forward.

Original steps
  1. Attach a rope to a pulley set at about head height and step back until the cable is tight
  2. Hold one end in each hand with your thumbs pointing back
  3. Pull the rope toward your face, splitting your hands apart as it comes
  4. Finish with your hands beside your ears and your elbows level with your shoulders
  5. Return slowly, letting the shoulder blades reach forward at the end

Original purpose

Lying face down takes the lower back out of it entirely, so the small muscles between and below the shoulder blades have to lift the weight themselves. Raising the arms in a Y is the shape that reaches the lower trapezius, which almost nothing else does.

Original steps
  1. Set a bench to a low incline and lie face down with your chest on the pad
  2. Hold a light dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down, thumbs up
  3. Keep your neck long and your chin gently tucked
  4. Raise both arms up and out to form a Y with your body, thumbs leading
  5. Stop at shoulder height or a little above, then lower slowly

1435. Dumbbell Laying 30 Degree Shrug

ShouldersP2
Mismatch matrix

P2 · PRIOR_REAUDIT · Purpose/Steps
This card was not materially changed in REV2 for the prior finding(s); the previous finding remains open.
Action: Use neutral wording about the movement/muscles; avoid claiming one exercise reverses a lifestyle/postural problem without assessment.

Original purpose

Lying on an incline changes the direction of the load, so the shrug pulls the shoulder blades down and back instead of straight up. That is the direction that helps posture rather than the one that builds a thicker neck.

Original steps
  1. Set a bench to about thirty degrees and lie face down on it, chest supported
  2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with the arms hanging straight down
  3. Let your shoulder blades slide forward and apart at the start
  4. Draw the blades back and down toward your hips, arms staying straight
  5. Hold the position for a second, then lower under control
Proposed variant
Purpose: Trains the shoulder musculature through the Dumbbell Laying 30 Degree Shrug movement. Use a comfortable range and stop if you feel sharp or pinching pain.
Steps: No deterministic step rewrite required. Follow the Action note above for judgment-based changes.

1436. Dumbbell Laying Silverback Shrug

ShouldersP1
Mismatch matrix

P1 · JOINT_LOCK · Steps
Uses 'lock' at a knee/elbow, which can be interpreted as forceful hyperextension.
Action: Use 'fully extend without forceful hyperextension' or simply 'straighten under control'.

Original purpose

A face-down shrug that targets the middle of the trapezius — the section between the shoulder blades that holds them against the ribs. Weak there is why shoulders drift forward and why heavy pulling feels unstable.

Original steps
  1. Lie face down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand
  2. Let the arms hang straight down and allow the shoulder blades to spread apart
  3. Keep the elbows locked straight for the whole movement
  4. Squeeze the shoulder blades toward each other without bending the arms
  5. Pause at the fully squeezed position, then release slowly
Proposed variant

1463. Dumbbell Shoulder Extension

ShouldersP1
Mismatch matrix

P1 · PRIOR_REAUDIT · Purpose/Steps
This card was not materially changed in REV2 for the prior finding(s); the previous finding remains open.
Action: Replace with 'can', 'may', 'often', 'a useful option', or a specific observable training effect.; Use neutral wording about the movement/muscles; avoid claiming one exercise reverses a lifestyle/postural problem without assessment.

P1 · JOINT_LOCK · Steps
Uses 'lock' at a knee/elbow, which can be interpreted as forceful hyperextension.
Action: Use 'fully extend without forceful hyperextension' or simply 'straighten under control'.

P2 · SPINE_CUE · Steps
Uses 'flat/straight back' as a rigid dynamic cue; for loaded hinges/rows/planks a stable neutral spine is clearer.
Action: Use 'brace and maintain a stable/neutral spine' unless flat contact with a support is the actual goal.

P2 · POSTURE_CAUSAL · Purpose
Attributes posture/tightness to a single lifestyle cause or implies one exercise corrects it without assessment.
Action: Describe the movement/muscles and mobility target; avoid diagnosing a posture problem or promising to reverse it.

P2 · SUPERLATIVE_CLAIM · Purpose
Uses a best/most/only/comparative claim without a defined population, outcome or evidence threshold.
Action: State the direct training effect, or soften to 'can', 'may', 'often', 'a useful option' and define the comparison if it matters.

Original purpose

Taking the arms behind the body works the back of the shoulder and the lats through a range that almost nothing else uses. It directly opens the front of the shoulders, which is where the tightness from sitting collects.

Original steps
  1. Stand tall with a light dumbbell in each hand, arms by your sides, palms facing back
  2. Keep the ribs down and the chest open, without arching the lower back
  3. Sweep both arms straight back behind you with the elbows locked
  4. Go only as far as the shoulders allow without the chest collapsing forward
  5. Return to your sides slowly, resisting the weight the whole way
Proposed variant
Purpose: Trains the shoulder musculature through the Dumbbell Shoulder Extension movement. Use a comfortable range and stop if you feel sharp or pinching pain.
Steps: No deterministic step rewrite required. Follow the Action note above for judgment-based changes.

Original purpose

Builds the side of the shoulder and the upper trapezius together. Using one arm lets the elbow travel on the path your own shoulder prefers, which is what makes this safer than the two-handed barbell version many people find pinching.

Original steps
  1. Stand tall with a dumbbell in one hand resting against the front of your thigh
  2. Put the other hand on your hip and keep your shoulders level
  3. Pull the dumbbell straight up close to your body, leading with the elbow
  4. Stop when the elbow reaches shoulder height — no higher
  5. Lower slowly to the thigh, then finish the set and change arms

1651. Foam Roller Back

Stretching - MobilityP2
Mismatch matrix

P2 · PRIOR_REAUDIT · Purpose/Steps
This card was not materially changed in REV2 for the prior finding(s); the previous finding remains open.

Original purpose

Rolling the upper back restores the extension that sitting takes away, which is what lets you hold a bar overhead or keep the chest up in a squat. Stay above the ribs — never roll the lower back.

Original steps
  1. Lie on your back with a foam roller across your upper back, below the shoulder blades
  2. Support your head with your hands and lift your hips off the floor
  3. Roll slowly up and down between the shoulder blades and the base of the neck
  4. Pause on any tight spot and breathe for a few seconds
  5. Stop at the bottom of the ribs — do not roll onto the lower back
Proposed variant
Purpose: Develops mobility in the areas used by the Foam Roller Back position. Move only to mild tension or slight discomfort, not sharp or radiating pain.

1878. Runners Lunge

YogaPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

Opens the front of the back hip and the inside of the front one, which is the pair that limits stride length in running. Ninety seconds of this before a run changes how the first kilometre feels.

Original steps
  1. From all fours, step one foot forward to the outside of the same-side hand
  2. Straighten the back leg and press through the heel or rest the knee down
  3. Lower onto your forearms or keep the hands flat, whichever you can hold
  4. Let the front hip sink toward the floor and keep the chest open
  5. Hold for thirty to sixty seconds, then change sides

1887. Yoga Flow Sequences Sun Salutations

YogaPASS
Mismatch matrix

PASS No targeted pattern issue detected by this audit.

Original purpose

A sequence rather than a single pose: it moves the whole spine through flexion and extension while warming the shoulders, hips and hamstrings. The most efficient general warm-up there is when you have five minutes and no equipment.

Original steps
  1. Stand tall, then reach both arms overhead on an inhale
  2. Fold forward over your legs, then lift halfway with a neutral spine
  3. Step or jump back to a plank, lower down, and lift the chest into a gentle backbend
  4. Push the hips up and back into a downward dog and hold for a breath
  5. Step the feet back to the hands, fold, and rise to standing — then repeat the round
